input.question: What position does Annerie Maria Magdalena Weber currently or formerly hold?

documents.text: As the sun set over the bustling streets of New Delhi, Annerie Maria Magdalena Weber, resplendent in her intricately embroidered sari, stepped out of the viceregal carriage and onto the worn stone steps of the Viceroy's House. The warm glow of the setting sun danced across her face, illuminating the determined set of her jaw and the piercing intensity of her gaze. It was a look that had served her well in the rough-and-tumble world of South African politics, where she had cut her teeth as a member of the National Assembly. Now, as the newly appointed Governor-General of India, Annerie was determined to bring her unique blend of pragmatism and passion to the role. As she made her way through the crowded reception hall, she was greeted by a sea of dignitaries, each one vying for her attention. But Annerie's eyes were fixed on the figure of Sir Reginald Pembroke, the outgoing Governor-General, who stood stiffly at attention, his face a mask of propriety. "Sir Reginald," Annerie said, her voice like honey and steel, "I trust you're prepared to brief me on the state of affairs in this great nation?" Pembroke's eyes flickered, ever so slightly, before he bowed his head in deference. "Of course, Your Excellency. I have prepared a comprehensive report on the current situation in India. Shall we proceed to the study?" As they made their way through the labyrinthine corridors of the Viceroy's House, Annerie's mind was already racing ahead, her thoughts turning to the complex web of alliances and rivalries that had defined British India for centuries. She knew that her appointment was seen as a bold move by the British government, a nod to the growing influence of the dominions in the Empire. But Annerie was determined to prove herself more than just a token appointment. She was here to make a difference, to leave her mark on this ancient and troubled land. And as she settled into the ornate chair behind the Governor-General's desk, Annerie felt a sense of history weighing upon her shoulders. She was the first woman to hold this position, the first South African, and the first member of the National Assembly to be appointed to this exalted role. The weight of expectation was crushing, but Annerie was undaunted.
